questions.question: Name the four core industrial regions and explain why Gauteng stays dominant despite having no port and no major river.
questions.expected_answer: Gauteng (PWV), Durban–Pinetown, Port Elizabeth–Uitenhage and the South-Western Cape. Gauteng dominates because Witwatersrand gold pulled capital, labour, railways and coal-fired power onto the plateau; the missing water was engineered in through the Vaal Dam and Lesotho Highlands scheme; and agglomeration then took over — deep skills, Africa's richest market, converging transport and thousands of linked firms keep the region on top even as the gold runs out. Industrial regions outlive their reasons.

questions.question: Outline the Port Elizabeth–Uitenhage region's location factors, main activities and chief weakness.
questions.expected_answer: Location: the natural harbour on Algoa Bay, railways inland to the Karoo's wool and hides, flat affordable land, decisive investment by global vehicle makers (Volkswagen at Uitenhage/Kariega, historically Ford and General Motors), and now the deep-water port at Ngqura. Activities: vehicle assembly (Volkswagen, Isuzu) with a dense component belt — catalytic converters a speciality — plus tyres, textiles, food processing and port logistics. Chief weakness: dependence on one industry, so slumps in world car demand shake the whole region — compounded by drought risk, load-shedding and the surrounding province's poverty.

questions.question: Distinguish SDIs from IDZs, give the flagship example of each, and state the balanced verdict on their success.
questions.expected_answer: An SDI is a line policy — investment upgrades a whole corridor of road and rail so activity develops along the route; flagship: the Maputo Development Corridor from Gauteng to Maputo's harbour. An IDZ (now inside the SEZ framework) is a point policy — a fenced, serviced estate at a port or airport with incentives and duty-free inputs for export manufacturing; flagship: Coega beside Ngqura, with East London, Richards Bay, Dube TradePort and Saldanha Bay as the other named zones. Verdict: genuine factories, jobs and freight have appeared, but at high cost per job and without breaking the four-region concentration — redistribution at the margin, not a redrawn map.
